title: Approval matrix, simulated canary and forensic rollback tool for Optimize suggestions
creator: Ethan Ross
description: Build a combined system to safely auto-apply Optimize recommendations (batching and prefix/KV caching configs) that provides: 1) a parameterized approval matrix which maps recommendation risk tiers to required approvers and SLAs, 2) a simulated canary runner that replays traffic in a sandbox and produces cost/latency/regression signals before any live rollout, and 3) a forensic rollback tool that automates safe revert and generates postmortem artifacts and audit logs for compliance. The design must integrate with Console rollouts, the Optimize recommender, and existing observability dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Approval matrix UI and API exist and enforce that P2/P3 recs can be auto-applied but P0/P1 require at least one SRE and one PM approval
Simulated canary runner accepts a workload snapshot, applies a recommendation in sandbox, and outputs P95 latency delta, tokens-per-request delta, and error rate delta to the Optimize CI dashboard
Automated rollback triggers when simulated canary indicates >10% latency regression or live canary shows >5% error-rate increase for 5 minutes
Every auto-apply action creates an immutable audit record with approvers, config diffs, and links to simulation results
Forensic rollback tool can rehydrate the previous config, submit a revert PR to Dedicated/private config stores, and create an incident artifact in Confluence
E2E test coverage for approval matrix checks and simulation-to-live gating path included in CI
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design approval matrix data model, policy rules, and RBAC mapping with SRE/PM/Compliance
Phase 2: Implement simulated canary runner that can replay historical workload and compare metrics; add exporter to Optimize CI dashboard
Phase 3: Wire approval API into Optimize suggestions flow and Console rollout UI; add role-based approval workflows and temporal/timeboxed approvals
Phase 4: Implement automated revert triggers and the forensic rollback tool that generates PRs and incident artifacts
Phase 5: Run pilot with low-risk batching suggestions for two customers and iterate on thresholds
Phase 6: Gradual enablement for broader customers with documentation and runbook
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from simulated canary causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: keep simulation conservative; use multiple traffic snapshots and statistical tests.
Risk: Approval bottlenecks slow down cost savings. Mitigation: tier approvals by risk and allow auto-apply for low-risk recs with audit trail.
Risk: Incomplete observability for private deployments. Mitigation: require onboarded observability agent and minimum telemetry before auto-apply is allowed.
Risk: Regression in edge cases where batching increases tail latency. Mitigation: add per-route tail-latency checks and route-specific exemptions

Manual runbook verification with oncall SRE during pilot
rollback_playbook: 1) Detect anomaly via live canary metrics or alert from Optimize CI
2) Mark rollout as paused and trigger automated revert job
3) Rehydrate previous config from audit blob and apply to target pool
4) Create incident artifact in Confluence with attached simulation and production traces
5) Notify stakeholders via PagerDuty and Slack channel #optimize-rollouts
6) Open follow-up ticket for root cause analysis and add to postmortem board
notes: Design decision: prefer explicit approver matrix over ML-based auto-approval for the initial launch to satisfy Compliance
We should reuse existing rollout primitives from Console to avoid duplicating state machines
Consider exposing a lightweight sandbox token so customers can opt into the simulated canary with their live traffic mirrors
